## Summary

This project was conducted in partnership with TVision, a leader in TV audience measurement, as part of the Rady MSBA Capstone. The goal was to design a media planning tool that helps advertisers maximize incremental reach by selecting optimal combinations of Linear TV and Connected TV (CTV) ad placements.

[Download Full Presentation (PDF)](capstone.pdf)

## Objectives

- Evaluate historic campaign performance using TVision panel data
- Build forecasting models for future campaign reach
- Recommend optimal media strategies based on advertiser goals

## Problem Context

As audiences increasingly shift from traditional linear TV to CTV platforms (like Netflix, Hulu, and YouTube), advertisers face challenges in avoiding redundant reach and budget waste. Planners need tools that:

- Quantify overlap in reach between platforms
- Predict **incremental reach** from CTV after a linear TV campaign
- Suggest cost-effective strategies by adjusting allocation across networks and apps


## Data Overview

TVision provided campaign data from **5 recent quarters**, including:

- Ad impressions on linear and CTV platforms
- Timestamps (day, time, duration)
- Viewer demographics and attention signals
- Platform metadata (network/app ID)

| Field                    | Description                              |
|-------------------------|------------------------------------------|
| `Viewer_ID`             | Unique anonymous viewer                  |
| `Channel/Platform`      | Linear TV or CTV app                     |
| `Ad_Timestamp`          | Date + time of ad view                   |
| `Attention_Flag`        | Viewer was attentive (Yes/No)            |
| `Campaign_ID`           | Unique campaign strategy identifier      |
| `Target_Demographic`    | Age, gender, household metadata          |
